sectionTitle: What changed beyond the sales office

primary.headline: Hays County Secures Over $39 Million for Railroad Overpass at Centerpoint Road
primary.summary: The Federal Railroad Administration's Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail Program awarded Hays County a $39.23 million grant (80% of project cost) to build a grade-separated overpass over the Union Pacific Railroad crossing at Centerpoint Road, extending from I-35 to FM 2439/Hunter Road. Hays County and Union Pacific will fund the remaining 20% (about $9.81 million). Preliminary engineering and schematic design are complete; right-of-way acquisition and final design are underway. County officials cited faster, safer emergency-response routing as a key driver.
primary.buyerImplication: This is new, corridor-specific infrastructure investment in one of the fastest-growing residential submarkets in Central Texas (Kyle/Hays County, home to active communities from Blackburn Homes, DRB Homes, Century Communities, and others). A grade-separated crossing removing train-vehicle conflicts on a road connecting I-35 to FM 2439 signals continued public investment in the corridor's road capacity and emergency-response times, though the article does not give a construction start or completion date -- the project is still in the right-of-way/design phase, so it won't resolve current at-grade crossing delays anytime soon.
primary.buyerAction: Buyers evaluating new-construction communities near Centerpoint Road, I-35, or FM 2439 in the Kyle/Hays County area should ask their builder or the county for the project's expected construction timeline before assuming near-term relief from rail-crossing delays, and should factor current at-grade crossing wait times into daily-commute expectations until construction begins.
primary.confidence: High confidence -- Community Impact reporting, published 2026-09-01 (same-day). Replaces the Spectrum News 1 incentives-trend piece after a 20-run hold. Note: the source article does not itself discuss home buying or named residential developments -- the new-construction connection is NHD's editorial framing of corridor growth plus infrastructure investment, and the article gives no construction timeline.
